descriptionChirho: Aramaic verb in Qal stem meaning 'to be able, to have the power or capacity to do something.' Used exclusively in Daniel (Dan 2:10, 2:27, 2:47, 3:17, 3:29, 4:18, 4:37, 5:16, 6:4, 6:20). All inflections (imperfect, participle, perfect) and qere/ketiv variants express the same basic modal sense of ability or capacity, corresponding to Hebrew יָכֹל. Multilingual glosses consistently render as 'pouvoir' (fra), 'können' (deu), 'poder' (spa), 'समर्थ/सकना' (hin), confirming a unified sense.

Aramaic verb in Qal stem meaning 'to prevail against, to overcome, to gain mastery over.' In Dan 7:21, the little horn 'prevailed against' (וְיָכְלָה) the saints, where the sense shifts from mere ability to active domination and victory. Arabic glosses render وَغَلَبَهُمْ 'and he overcame them,' Hindi जीत रहा था 'was winning,' Korean 이기고있었다 'was defeating,' and Spanish los vencía 'was conquering them,' all confirming a distinct sense of military/spiritual overcoming rather than simple ability.
